blocks.text: Deliver secrets as files under /run/secrets; the app reads the file, so the value stays out of docker inspect's Env list and isn't inherited by child processes.

blocks.code:
services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password   # official images support *_FILE
    secrets: [db_password]
  api:
    secrets: [db_password, openai_api_key]
secrets:
  db_password:
    file: ./secrets/db_password.txt
  openai_api_key:
    environment: OPENAI_API_KEY

blocks.text: With `secrets_dir="/run/secrets"`, pydantic-settings loads `/run/secrets/openai_api_key` into the field `openai_api_key`.

rows: `echo "pw" > file` adds a newline; Postgres uses it as-is, the app may strip it
Plain-Compose secrets are bind mounts: host mode/UID apply
Make the file readable by the container user
Not a vault: unencrypted on disk, no rotation or audit
Swarm/K8s secrets or Vault/cloud secret managers

blocks.text: Support `X_FILE` in your own app: read the file if set, else fall back to `X`. The same image then works with env in dev and files in prod.

Q: "How do you pass a database password to containers without env vars?" A: "As a Compose (or Kubernetes) secret mounted at /run/secrets/<name>, with POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE for the official image and pydantic-settings secrets_dir or a _FILE reader in the app. Watch for trailing newlines and file permissions."
